text:
raj: Heads-up — discovered a gap in how our DB snapshots and blobstore archives are encrypted when copied between regions. Backup uploader role currently uses a shared service account that holds an old CMK grant. Need guidance on RBAC changes + audit logging to ensure restores won't break. TL;DR: how do we rotate the CMK + PRUNE old grants without losing restore capability?

olivia: Oof. Can you paste the uploader role IAM snippet and the KMS policy?

raj: Pasting minimal example:```json
// uploader-role-policy.json
{
  "bindings": [
    { "role": "roles/storage.objectAdmin", "members": ["serviceAccount:backups-uploader@redwood-prod.iam.gserviceaccount.com"] }
  ]
}
```And KMS grants: we have a list of grants tied to the CMK per-region; some expired, some have schedule-rotation labels.

sam: Two quick points: 1) Before rotating or pruning, add a short-lived grant to a temporary CMK (or a new CMK alias) and test restore ops from a staging snapshot. 2) Ensure audit logs capture KMS.Decrypt and storage.objects.get for that service account so we can prove restores succeed.

kevin: Also check that our snapshot metadata contains the key version id (not just CMK alias). We had a previous incident where alias pointed to new key and old snapshots lacked version id -> decrypt failure.

raj: Good call. Right now metadata only stores alias and region. That's bad. Will add key_version in metadata.

olivia: For RBAC change, prefer additive rollout: create new service account backups-uploader-v2, grant it storage.objectAdmin + kms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter on the new key, wire it into the uploader in a canary region for 24h, verify restore path, then swap. Keep the old SA around for 7 days but revoke grants gradually.

sam: Add to that: update audit pipeline to flag any failed KMS.Decrypt events and correlate with snapshot-id tags — produce an alert if any restore fails due to key mismatch. Also log: principalEmail, keyName, keyVersion, operation, snapshotId.

encops-bot: DEPLOYMENT NOTE: please run the following on canary before full rollout:
1) generate test snapshot with key_version set
2) run restore with backups-uploader-v2 creds
3) verify object checksums + decrypt success

kevin: For prune timing: run a dry-run that lists objects referencing the old key version. Use: ```bash
gsutil ls -L gs://backups-prod/** | jq '. | select(.metadata.key_version=="v1")'
``` Mark those snapshots, copy them to new envelope if needed, then revoke grant.

raj: Sounds actionable. Who wants to own the runbook update? I can do the metadata and canary wiring. Need someone for the audit pipeline changes and the dry-run.

olivia: I can take audit pipeline (add fields + alert).

sam: I'll own the dry-run and the key-copy script.

raj: Thanks — I'll start a PR for uploader-v2 RBAC + metadata changes and ping reviewers. Will also schedule a short drill with oncall. :thumbsup:
